d: We are looking for a highly accomplished, deeply technical Senior Forward Deployment Engineer to serve as the dedicated technical engine and trusted advisor for a strategic enterprise client.

In this role, you will not just consult from the sidelines; you will sit on the front lines. You will own the technical relationship end-to-end, serving as the client’s go-to technical expert, architecting complex Proofs of Concept (PoCs), building hands-on demos, and solving complex architecture and integration challenges in real time.

If you thrive at the intersection of production-grade engineering, complex problem-solving, and high-impact client engagement, this role is for you. If you're not scared to use AI to help guide your, and our, work, this role is for you. If you're excited at the prospect of stepping across traditional role boundaries towards things like building agents, product ownership and requirements analysis, this role is for you.
Dedicated Technical Advisory: Act as the primary, high-touch technical authority and advisor for a key enterprise customer, translating complex technical capability into strategic client value.

Account Expansion & Sales Vigour: Proactively identify technical gaps and new business opportunities within the account. Partner closely with the presales team to put together future architectures, pitch new solutions, and drive the expansion of our platform.
Rapid Prototyping & PoCs: Scope, design, and build custom demos, production-grade prototypes, and Proofs of Concept (PoCs) directly tailored to the customer’s unique ecosystem and edge cases.

Architecture & Integration: Work hands-on with the customer's engineering, security, and infrastructure teams to design seamless deployment pipelines, custom integrations, and data flows, with a heavy emphasis on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environments.
Real-time Technical Problem Solving: Unblock customer engineering teams by debugging complex deployment, infrastructure, integration, or performance issues on the fly.

Product Feedback Loop: Serve as the direct bridge between the customer’s engineering requirements and our internal Product & Core Engineering teams, advocating for features that drive enterprise adoption.
Senior Engineering Track Record: 10+ years of hands-on experience in software engineering, backend systems, cloud architecture, or site reliability engineering (SRE).
Hands-on Coding: Strong proficiency in modern enterprise programming languages (e.g. Python, Java, TypeScript/Node.js, or even Rust or Golang).
Cloud & Infrastructure Mastery: Deep experience with GCP cloud platform, containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and modern CI/CD practices.
Integration & Systems Design: Proven ability to architect REST/gRPC APIs, microservices, enterprise security integrations (SAML, OAuth, VPCs), and data pipelines.
q: Executive Presence: Ability to switch effortlessly between white-boarding code with senior developers and presenting architectural strategies to CTOs and VP-level stakeholders.
Technical Ownership: High autonomy, grit, and a strong sense of ownership: you don't wait for answers; you invent solutions.
Empathy & Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with a track record of building deep trust with client engineering teams.
Experience in specialized domains relevant to our tech stack (e.g., AI/ML infrastructure, distributed systems, high-throughput data processing, or cybersecurity).
Prior experience in forward deployment, technical pre-sales, or high-touch technical account management at a high-growth SaaS or deep-tech enterprise company.
Track record working within financial services, payments, or the broader FinTech ecosystem, with a solid understanding of the sector's unique security, regulatory, and high-transaction requirements.
Experience with other cloud platforms like Azure, AWS and Huawei.
What Success Looks Like in Year 1
First 90 Days: Build deep technical trust with the customer’s core technical team, fully understand their tech stack and architecture, and ship your first production integration or PoC.
6 Months: Become the indispensable "go-to" technical expert for the account, reducing time-to-value for new client initiatives and driving architectural alignment.
1 Year: Expand the customer’s technical footprint with our solutions through successful PoCs, seamless system stability, and proactive feature delivery.

d: Set high expectations which inspire, motivate and challenge pupils:
Establish a safe and stimulating environment for pupils, rooted in mutual respect
Set goals that stretch and challenge pupils of all backgrounds, abilities and dispositions
Demonstrate consistently the positive attitudes, values and behaviour which are expected of pupils
Promote positive progress and outcomes with/for pupils through:
Accountability of pupils’ attainment, progress and outcomes
Awareness of pupils’ capabilities and their prior knowledge, and plan teaching to build on these
Guidance of pupils to reflect on the progress they have made and their emerging needs
Knowledge and understanding of how pupils learn and how this impacts on teaching
Encouraging pupils to take a responsible and conscientious attitude to their own work and study
Demonstrate good subject and curriculum knowledge through:
Sound knowledge of the relevant subject(s) and curriculum areas, foster and maintain pupils’ interest in the subject, and address misunderstandings
Critical understanding of developments in the subject and curriculum areas, and promote the value of scholarship
Demonstrate an understanding of and take responsibility for promoting high standards of literacy, articulacy and the correct use of Standard English, whatever the teacher’s specialist subject
If teaching early reading, demonstrate a clear understanding of systematic synthetic phonics
If teaching early mathematics, demonstrate a clear understanding of appropriate teaching strategies
Impart knowledge and develop understanding through effective use of lesson time
Promote a love of learning and pupil’s intellectual curiosity
Set homework when appropriate and plan other out-of-class activities to consolidate and extend the knowledge and understanding pupils have acquired
Reflect systematically on the effectiveness of lessons and approaches to teaching
Contribute to the design and provision of an engaging curriculum within the relevant subject area(s)
Adapt teaching to respond to the strengths and needs of all pupils through:
The ability to differentiate appropriately, using approaches which enable pupils to be taught effectively
A sound understanding of how a range of factors can inhibit pupils’ ability to learn, and how best to overcome these
Awareness of the physical, social and intellectual development of pupils, and know how to adapt teaching to support pupils’ education at different stages of development

A clear understanding of the needs of all pupils, including those with special educational needs; those of high ability; those with English as an additional language; those with disabilities; and be able to use and evaluate distinctive teaching approaches to engage and support them
Make accurate and productive use of assessment:
Assess the relevant subject and curriculum areas, including statutory assessment requirements
Make use of formative and summative assessment to secure pupils’ progress
Use relevant data to monitor progress, set targets, and plan subsequent lessons
Give pupils regular feedback, both orally and through accurate marking, and encourage pupils to respond positively to the feedback
Manage behaviour effectively to ensure a good and safe learning environment:

Have clear rules and routines for behaviour in classrooms, and take responsibility for promoting good and courteous behaviour both in classrooms and around the school, in accordance with the school’s behaviour policy
Have high expectations of behaviour, and establish a framework for discipline with a range of strategies, using praise, sanctions and rewards consistently and fairly
Manage classes effectively, using approaches which are appropriate to pupils’ needs in order to involve and motivate them
Maintain good relationships with pupils, exercise appropriate authority, and act decisively when necessary
